classification.difficultyReason: Reduce 100 hours modulo 12, then count backwards and wrap past 12 to interpret the displayed hour.

content.prompt: The clock below shows 3 o’clock. What time did it show 100 hours ago?

spec.description: Unshaded analogue clock with numerals 1–12, twelve hour ticks and longer cardinal ticks. Minute hand points to 12; shorter hour hand points to 3. Decorative cyan face omitted under house style.
spec.mathematics: A twelve-hour clock displaying exactly 3 o’clock.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied starting time is visible; the requested earlier time is not shown.

answer.worked:
The clock repeats every 12 hours.
$$100=8\times12+4.$$
Going back 100 hours therefore gives the same displayed time as going back 4 hours.
$$\begin{align*}3-4&=-1\\3-4&\equiv11\pmod{12}.\end{align*}$$
The clock showed 11 o’clock.
